newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soybean traders in the dark over U.S. deal.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soybean traders in the dark over U.S. deal.

text.p: Brazilian soybean traders said they were unaware of any negotiations being conducted with U.S. soybean crusher Owensboro Grain Co after the company said today it was negotiating to buy soybeans from South America.
In March, Owensboro bought 150,000 tonnes of optional origin soybeans and one of these cargoes was shipped from Brazil.
"It seems a bit strange as I'd heard that they were not looking to buy any beans from South America, either from Brazil or Argentina," one trader said.
"From what I'd heard about the last cargo, the oil content was a little lower than they had been looking for," he added.
While the Owensboro company official would not confirm tonnage, U.S. exporters said the deal involved up to two cargoes (100,000 tonnes) of soybeans.
Shipping sources in Paranagua, the country's key grains port, also said they had not heard of any enquiries in the soybean freight market for Brazil to the U.S. Gulf.
